correctness.rationale: For every fixed theta_i,a_i>0, H_theta is a strictly increasing diffeomorphism with two-sided linear bounds on its inverse. Direct integration gives Z_kappa~log(kappa)/kappa. Dominated convergence yields E[X_i]~A_i/log(kappa) and E[X_i^2]~B_i/log(kappa). The mixed moment is O(1/kappa) by an explicit split integral, so covariance~ -A_1*A_2/log(kappa)^2 and Pearson~ -A_1*A_2/sqrt(B_1*B_2)/log(kappa). Conditional exponential monotonicity gives strict negativity for every kappa>0. Rescaled logarithms -log(Y_i)/log(kappa) converge jointly to (U,1-U), proving copula limit W and both rank limits. Finite moment diagnostics and fixed-seed conditional simulations were actually executed from the included code; they are nonessential numerical cross-checks.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: An existing negative-covariance assertion does not imply Pearson correlation returns to zero, and finite-parameter correlation tables do not imply the exact logarithmic coefficient. Those limits follow here from new uniform logarithmic-exponent scaling and dominated moment asymptotics. Underlying formulas, distribution and sampler are not claimed.

value.rationale: For bivariate dependent lifetime modeling, the distinction between rank and linear dependence is material: stronger conditional coupling drives essentially perfect reversed ordering while Pearson correlation attenuates rather than increases. The sharp logarithmic coefficient depends explicitly on the physically modeled inverse-Lindley hazard and explains the slow finite-coupling behavior, not merely a qualitative limiting statement. It can prevent false interpretation of a small Pearson coefficient as weak dependence, and identifies a genuine nonmonotone Pearson phase along a natural model parameter.
